summary: Thurston County lookout site in Capitol State Forest: 1930s tower and cabin, now gone; reached by trail, with a gated road to the summit.

facts.design: Tower with cabin per the register; a 1942 state inventory (cited by willhiteweb.com) calls it a groundhouse lookout
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin are gone; the washingtonlookouts listing marks it removed; a 2022 hike report describes the site without remains

access.note: Hiking trails reach the summit, shared with bicycles; the forest road is gated and driveable only when the gate is open

visit.drive_up: Forest road to the summit, about 2.5 miles past the gate, when the gate is open
visit.trail_note: Trails in Capitol State Forest shared with bicycles; motorized bikes May through November

events.note: Built in the 1930s (decade only in sources); willhiteweb.com places it after 1934; year 1935 is a placeholder for ordering only
A 1942 state lookout inventory calls it a groundhouse lookout (cited by willhiteweb.com)
Registered January 19, 2012; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com describe a tower and cabin; willhiteweb.com cites a 1942 state inventory calling it a groundhouse lookout. The story reports both; the brief's kind 'tower' is kept because two sources say tower.
All sources give only the 1930s. willhiteweb.com narrows the build to after 1934 from the October 1934 photos, which it says were taken before any structure existed.

notes_for_editor: Build year is known only as the 1930s; the after-1934 narrowing rests on willhiteweb.com's reading of the panorama photos. No removal year, staffing, or fire sources found. The 1942 inventory is cited second-hand via willhiteweb.com and was not read directly. The 2022 hike report describes the summit as the site without any remains. Access level 'public' rests on the trail description and the gated-road note; the brief's access 'unknown' was updated for that reason.
